title: Nhà ở xã hội và hòa nhập · Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some societies are considering requiring new housing developments to include affordable homes. What problems could this create, and what measures could be taken to address them?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

outline.purpose: Chỉ phân tích khó khăn do chính biện pháp được đề xuất gây ra và ghép mỗi khó khăn với cách xử lý đúng cơ chế; không dùng đoạn lợi ích thay phần giải pháp. Trường hợp Nhà ở xã hội và hòa nhập: Nhà giá phải chăng tại khu có trường và giao thông tốt mở tiếp cận việc làm, không chỉ tạo số căn hộ. Nhân viên y tế ở gần bệnh viện nối vị trí nhà với thời gian và khả năng làm việc. Giới hạn: Không coi ở cùng địa chỉ là hòa nhập. Cửa vào tách biệt hoặc không được dùng tiện ích tạo phân tầng ngay trong dự án; tính “affordable” còn cần gắn thu nhập người dự kiến ở.
outline.content: Affordable homes within new developments can open access to good locations, although excessive obligations or segregated facilities can undermine both construction and social inclusion. The main risks are stalled construction and unequal access within completed schemes; predictable viability rules and enforceable shared-facility rights must protect both the supply of homes and the inclusion they are meant to achieve.

Nhà giá phải chăng tại khu có trường và giao thông tốt mở tiếp cận việc làm, không chỉ tạo số căn hộ. Nhân viên y tế ở gần bệnh viện nối vị trí nhà với thời gian và khả năng làm việc.

grammar.name: Đối lập hai mệnh đề
grammar.example: Affordable homes within new developments can open access to good locations, although excessive obligations or segregated facilities can undermine both construction and social inclusion.
grammar.why: Trong câu mở, although nối lợi ích dự kiến với giới hạn thực hiện cụ thể. Đưa rõ hai kiểu thất bại khác nhau: dự án không xây và dự án xây nhưng vẫn phân tầng; nhờ đó phản biện không bị thu hẹp thành một vấn đề chi phí chung.

paragraphs: Affordable homes within new developments can open access to good locations, although excessive obligations or segregated facilities can undermine both construction and social inclusion. The main risks are stalled construction and unequal access within completed schemes; predictable viability rules and enforceable shared-facility rights must protect both the supply of homes and the inclusion they are meant to achieve.

Poorly designed requirements can make some developments financially unviable or produce segregated entrances. If obligations are set without regard to project costs, developers may postpone construction, reducing total supply. Alternatively, a scheme may meet its numerical target while giving lower-income residents inferior entrances or facilities, preserving exclusion within an apparently mixed neighbourhood. An affordable flat improves inclusion only if its occupants can use the neighbourhood's services and shared facilities on comparable terms with other residents.

Published viability assessments should establish obligations before construction, and access rules should apply to shared entrances and facilities so that poorer residents receive more than a nominal address. Rules should be predictable and require comparable access to shared facilities. Viability checks should be transparent, while comparable access to entrances and facilities prevents a nominally mixed development from institutionalising a lower status for poorer residents. Developers can account for stable obligations when assessing a project, whereas unexpected changes after costs are committed make delay more likely and weaken the intended increase in housing supply. After completion, inspections should check residents’ actual use of common facilities, because a contract promising inclusion is inadequate if access cards or separate rules continue to exclude poorer households. Planning rules should assess the number of viable homes delivered and residents' effective access, rather than celebrate nominally mixed development that preserves segregation.
Inclusion requires homes that are actually built and residents who can share local opportunities; a quota achieves little if it stops construction or creates second-class access.

Viability checks should be transparent, while comparable access to entrances and facilities prevents a nominally mixed development from institutionalising a lower status for poorer residents. Developers can account for stable obligations when assessing a project, whereas unexpected changes after costs are committed make delay more likely and weaken the intended increase in housing supply. After completion, inspections should check residents’ actual use of common facilities, because a contract promising inclusion is inadequate if access cards or separate rules continue to exclude poorer households. Planning rules should assess the number of viable homes delivered and residents' effective access, rather than celebrate nominally mixed development that preserves segregation.
paragraphs.why: Yêu cầu quá sức tài chính có thể làm dự án không xây, giảm nguồn cung. Quy tắc dự đoán được giúp tính chi phí từ đầu; quyền dùng tiện ích ngang nhau xử lý loại trừ bên trong.

options: The main risks are stalled construction and unequal access within completed schemes; predictable viability rules and enforceable shared-facility rights must protect both the supply of homes and the inclusion they are meant to achieve.

I completely support requiring new housing developments to include affordable homes in every circumstance, regardless of its consequences.
